name: Louisiana
agency: Louisiana Office of Motor Vehicles (OMV), Department of Public Safety
permitAge: 15 (learner's permit), after an approved 38-hour driver education course, knowledge test and vision screening

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 15 at night (state GDL law card)
teen.nightLimit: Intermediate license: no driving 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. unless with a licensed parent or guardian, a licensed adult 21+, or a licensed sibling 18+
teen.passengerLimit: Intermediate license: no more than one passenger under 21 (immediate family exempt) from 6 p.m. to 5 a.m.
teen.phone: Learner's permit: no phone use, hands-free included (law card). All drivers: hand-held ban from Aug. 1, 2025 (HB 519); hands-free calls and navigation allowed; first offense up to $100, up to $250 in a school or construction zone.

notes: Learner supervisor: licensed adult 21 or older, or licensed sibling 18 or older (DPS Graduated Licensing PDF).
Intermediate license at 16 requires no at-fault crashes or moving violations on the permit, and a road skills test. Full Class E at 17.
Knowledge test: practice sites say 40 questions and 80 percent; one site says 20 questions and 75 percent, another 30 and 70 percent. Conflicting and not official, so exam fields are null.
Handbook: Class D and E Driver's Guide; Spanish edition reported as "Guia de Conductores Clases D y E" (form DPSMV2053) by dmv.org. No official PDF URL found.

Move over law expanded (WAFB, Aug. 2026) to disabled vehicles showing hazard lights, flashing lights or another warning device. Move away on multi-lane roads; slow down when a lane change is not possible.
School bus on divided highways (R.S. 32:80): current text not confirmed; no question written.
Phone ban enforcement: one source says warnings first and full enforcement from January 2026; one says it is a secondary offense. Not confirmed; no question on enforcement.
Research done with WebSearch only; official sites were unreachable from the sandbox (proxy 403).
